findings.title: Potential re-entrant deadlock and post-await null dereference in the active workout controller
findings.root_cause: discardLocalBackup awaits cancelWorkout from inside _enqueue; cancelWorkout re-enqueues on the same serialized future, so the outer operation awaits itself. Separately, state.workout is dereferenced after an await without re-checking.
findings.evidence: Static read reported by flutter-specialist in S3 delegation TEST C. Not reproduced in A0.
findings.expected_behavior: Discard-backup completes and the active-workout state settles.
findings.actual_behavior: Hypothesised: the enqueued future never resolves, isLoading stays true, UI hangs; the dereference throws if the workout was cleared during the await.
findings.impact: A user discarding a local backup while the backend is unreachable can be left with a hanging screen and an unusable in-progress workout. Server data is unaffected.
findings.proposed_remediation: Call the internal cancel operation from discardLocalBackup instead of the public enqueuing method; capture state.workout into a local before the await and re-check it after.
findings.regression_risk: Workout discard, cancel, backup restore, and session-resume paths.
missing_tests: discard while a request is pending
cancel invoked when state.workout is null
findings.verification_method: Fake repository whose cancel never completes; assert with a timeout that discard returns.

findings.title: Legacy completion path can award a workout twice
findings.root_cause: Two independent guards: workout_rewards primary key on workout_id (L226-227) and workouts.is_xp_calculated (L229). L230 still accepts status='completed' with is_xp_calculated=false, so a legacy row already awarded before the flag existed, without a workout_rewards row, is awarded again.
findings.evidence: Static read reported by supabase-specialist in S3 delegation TEST D. Population depends on production data, which this audit cannot read.
findings.expected_behavior: At most one award per workout id, ever.
findings.actual_behavior: Undetermined for pre-existing rows; the guard is demonstrably permissive.
findings.impact: Inflated XP, level, streak, and possibly duplicate quest rewards for a legacy cohort. Bounded by the 1000 XP cap at L255 but not prevented.
findings.proposed_remediation: Additive migration: backfill workout_rewards for completed workouts with is_xp_calculated=true, verify counts, then tighten L230 so completion without a rewards row is accepted only when the workout produced no progression.
findings.regression_risk: Replaying completion for legitimate legacy rows returns an error if the backfill is incomplete.
missing_tests: legacy row awarded without workout_rewards row
replay after backfill
depends_on: FND-DATA-001 verification requires a legacy-shaped fixture or a live database
findings.verification_method: Fixture row: workout status completed, is_xp_calculated=false, no workout_rewards row, non-zero prior XP. Call complete_workout twice.

findings.title: The stated XP write invariant is narrower than the implementation
findings.root_cause: Documentation states complete_workout is the only writer of XP, but initialize_user seeds total_xp/level/streak, sync_daily_data resets current_streak and manages quests, and switch_class writes user_classes.current_xp/level/is_graduated.
findings.evidence: Function-by-function read with line references reported by supabase-specialist in S3 delegation TEST D; matches the migration text reviewed at A0.
findings.expected_behavior: One invariant sentence that is true of the code.
findings.actual_behavior: Three functions outside the named path write progression state.
findings.impact: A reviewer applying the literal invariant would accept a change that adds a real second award path. Documentation-level defect with review and migration consequences.
findings.proposed_remediation: Restate as: complete_workout is the only path that GRANTS XP for a completed workout; initialize_user, sync_daily_data and switch_class initialise or recompute derived state and never grant an award. Update AGENTS.md section 4 and 9, ARCHITECTURE.md sections 4 and 7, PROJECT_CONTEXT.md.
findings.regression_risk: None at runtime; editorial inconsistency with documents quoting the old wording.
missing_tests: static documentation check that would fail on a new writer
depends_on: A4 must confirm no fourth writer exists
findings.verification_method: Grep every function body for writes to users.total_xp, users.level, streaks, quest_instances, user_classes.

findings.title: No agent can write docs/audit, so the audit cannot run under its own orchestrator
findings.root_cause: The orchestrator edit allowlist covers docs/planning and docs/agent-system only; no agent allowlist covers docs/audit. All other agents are scoped to code, schema, seeds, or presentation, and qa-reviewer and context-keeper cannot write at all.
findings.evidence: Permission blocks read directly from all seven agent files at A0. The A0 artifact writes succeeded only because the active agent is the built-in build agent, not the orchestrator.
findings.expected_behavior: The agent designated to coordinate the audit can persist audit state.
findings.actual_behavior: Every A0 artifact write would be denied under the orchestrator profile.
findings.impact: The audit program's operating model is unexecutable as configured. Work is currently persisted by an unintended agent, which weakens the scope guarantees the orchestrator exists to enforce.
findings.resolution: A0.1 (2026-10-28): one rule { action: edit, resource: docs/audit/*, effect: allow } added to gymlvl-orchestrator.md, after the existing edit allows. '*' matches across '/', so docs/audit/phases/ is covered too. Verified configuration-level: edit rules are * deny first, then docs/planning/*, docs/agent-system/*, docs/audit/*; shell (15), subagent (7), webfetch, websearch and external_directory unchanged; subagent(gymlvl-orchestrator) still rejected, proving mode=primary; server emitted agent.updated at 2026-10-28T07:06:41.988Z, one second after the write. End-to-end verification PASS (2026-10-28): a throwaway session launched with opencode-cli.exe run --agent gymlvl-orchestrator wrote app/.perm-probe-2.md, and the assertion was made from a different session (Test-Path -> True, Get-Content -> probe); the same session ran node --version, previously denied. D-024 then replaced the narrow docs/audit/* rule with full development access plus approval gates, so the allowlist described by this finding no longer exists. Evidence: docs/agent-system/ACCESS_POLICY.md sections 3-5.
findings.proposed_remediation: With approval, add an edit allow for docs/audit/* to gymlvl-orchestrator.md. Do not widen any other permission.
findings.regression_risk: One documentation directory becomes writable by one agent; no code, schema, or configuration reach.
missing_tests: configuration test asserting each program directory has an owner
findings.verification_method: Re-run an A0 artifact write under the orchestrator profile and observe it succeed.

findings.title: The canonical project-memory document is stale on its own baseline
findings.root_cause: Section 2 is titled 'Repository and current baseline' but records a fixed checkpoint SHA (17ca562), a fixed tracked-file count (511), and a 'pushed and verified at the checkpoint' statement as current fact. Three commits had landed at A0; seven have landed by A1. The same fixed-SHA-in-prose pattern appears in the AGENTS.md baseline line, the DECISIONS.md and MASTER_PLAN.md headers, the PROJECT_CONTEXT.md glossary, and two docs/agent-system reference documents.
findings.evidence: Measured at A0: git rev-parse --short HEAD = 9c8e142; git rev-list --count 17ca562..HEAD = 3; git ls-files = 538 tracked files. Re-measured at A1 (e8c7c8e): git rev-list --count 17ca562..HEAD = 7; git ls-files | Measure-Object = 548. context-keeper independently flagged AGENTS.md lines 6-9 at A0 close. A0.1 added a second instance: DECISIONS.md summary table stops at D-014 while sections D-015 to D-024 exist. A1 completed the inventory: 15 stale claims across nine documents, recorded in phases/A1_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10, with dated evidence blocks and stage records explicitly classified as not stale. Two non-staleness defects were found in the same pass: docs/planning/SESSION_HANDOFF.md:26 asserts 'force-push stays gated' (disproved by FND-GOV-004) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:43 lists two of the three current migrations.
findings.expected_behavior: The document of record for 'what is true now' matches the repository, or states the rule for deriving it.
findings.actual_behavior: Baseline is seven commits behind and the tracked-file count is 37 short.
findings.impact: A resuming session works from a stale baseline and re-derives facts that are already recorded. No runtime effect.
findings.proposed_remediation: Express the baseline as a rule ('main HEAD is authoritative; confirm with git rev-parse main') plus a dated last-observed SHA, and drop or date the file count. Apply once, in one pass over the 15 rows in phases/A1_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.
missing_tests: optional check comparing recorded SHA to git rev-parse HEAD
findings.verification_method: Re-read section 2 against git rev-parse HEAD and git ls-files after the fix.

findings.title: Shell permission matching inside a chained command is undocumented
findings.root_cause: The orchestrator allows the unbounded shell prefix cd *. If matching were a naive whole-string glob, a chained command would inherit the cd allowance and could reach the global Git floor.
findings.evidence: Observed at A0: a command of the form cd "D:\Projects\gymlvl"; git push origin main was denied by the global rule git push *, so the deny fired on a sub-command that was not at the start of the string. The matcher's segmentation rule remains undocumented in this repository.
findings.expected_behavior: An allow rule cannot be used to smuggle a command that another rule denies.
findings.actual_behavior: Appears to hold for deny rules; unverified for allow rules.
findings.impact: Unknown. If allow rules were evaluated per segment without the deny rules being re-evaluated, one agent could execute commands outside its allowlist.
findings.resolution: A0.1 (2026-10-28): disproved by the authoritative OpenCode V2 permissions documentation. A shell resource is a scanner-produced command string and compound commands may produce several resources, with last-match-wins per resource. 'cd X; git push' yields at least two resources: the 'cd *' allow covers the first, the global 'git push *' deny still applies to the second. This matches the observed S3 permission.rejected. No repository change required; retained with the disproof attached. Post-D-024 (2026-10-28): the 'cd *' allow no longer exists; the orchestrator carries no shell allowlist. The disproof stands; the recorded rule path is historical.
findings.proposed_remediation: None required. The matcher semantics are documented upstream in the OpenCode V2 permissions guide.
findings.verification_method: Resolved by documentation, not by a trial: OpenCode V2 permissions guide, section on matching and shell resource scanning.

findings.title: The Android release manifest declares no INTERNET permission
findings.origin: A1; already planned as TASK_BOARD.md section M1-02 (lines 172-182) but never registered as a finding
findings.root_cause: Flutter's template places android.permission.INTERNET in the debug and profile source-set manifests, not in main. Android's manifest merger combines main with the selected build type, so a release build receives main alone. No release source set exists.
findings.evidence: Get-ChildItem app\android\app\src -Recurse -Filter AndroidManifest.xml returns exactly three files (debug, main, profile); no src/release/ directory exists. Select-String INTERNET matches only debug:6 and profile:6. main lines 1-45 contain no uses-permission element. app/pubspec.yaml:47 depends on supabase_flutter, and every data path in app/lib is a network call.
findings.expected_behavior: A release artifact can reach Supabase.
findings.actual_behavior: The release manifest declares no network permission, so every socket call fails at runtime.
findings.impact: A release or internal-testing build is functionally unusable once the user leaves the first screen. The failure surfaces as a network error rather than a crash, so it can be misread as a backend outage. Release blocker for the only artifact class that ships.
findings.proposed_remediation: Add <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/> to app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. After verifying the merged release manifest, delete the now-redundant copies from debug/profile so the requirement lives in one place.
findings.regression_risk: Minimal: a normal permission cannot break the build. Recurrence risk is real, because a future reader sees INTERNET in debug and may remove it from main again.
missing_tests: merged release manifest assertion
flutter build apk --release in CI
app/test/release_config_test.dart
findings.verification_method: flutter build apk --release, then inspect app/build/app/intermediates/merged_manifests/release/AndroidManifest.xml or run aapt dump permissions. NOT RUN in A1: Android SDK availability unconfirmed and it writes build artifacts.

findings.title: The release build is signed with the debug keystore
findings.origin: A1; already planned as TASK_BOARD.md section M1-02
findings.root_cause: build.gradle.kts:37 assigns signingConfigs.getByName("debug") to the release build type. This is the Flutter template default, retained unchanged.
findings.evidence: Select-String on app/android/app/build.gradle.kts: 'signingConfig = signingConfigs.getByName("debug")' at line 37, inside the release build type block.
findings.expected_behavior: Release artifacts are signed with a project-held release key.
findings.actual_behavior: Release artifacts are signed with the well-known public debug key.
findings.impact: Google Play rejects an artifact signed with the debug key, so the app cannot be distributed. A side-loaded build is trivially re-signable by anyone, breaking update authenticity and permitting impersonation.
findings.proposed_remediation: Add a key.properties-driven signingConfigs.create("release") with a gitignored keystore path, falling back to the debug config only when the properties file is absent so local debug builds keep working. Setup steps require user-held credentials and belong in a Vietnamese guide (AGENTS.md section 0.1C).
findings.regression_risk: A misconfigured key.properties breaks local release builds; the fallback keeps the failure scoped to release builds.
missing_tests: release artifact signature assertion
findings.verification_method: flutter build appbundle --release, then keytool -printcert -jarfile on the artifact; the certificate must not read CN=Android Debug. NOT RUN in A1.

findings.title: The platform display name is the Flutter template default
findings.origin: A1; already planned as TASK_BOARD.md section M1-02
findings.root_cause: Both platform manifests still carry the values Flutter's template generates: android:label="app", CFBundleDisplayName=App, CFBundleName=app. The in-app brand is 'GymLevel' (app.dart:21, app_en.arb appTitle).
findings.evidence: Direct read of both files; MaterialApp title is the literal 'GymLevel' at app/lib/app.dart:21 and appTitle is 'GymLevel' in app_en.arb.
findings.expected_behavior: The app appears as GymLevel on the launcher and in OS settings.
findings.actual_behavior: It appears as 'app' on Android and 'App' on iOS.
findings.impact: Cosmetic and branding only. Listed because it lives in the same two files as the two release-blocking defects and would otherwise be re-found after they are fixed.
findings.proposed_remediation: Set android:label="GymLevel", CFBundleDisplayName="GymLevel", CFBundleName="gymlvl" (iOS CFBundleName is limited to 15 characters; 'gymlvl' is safe).
missing_tests: label assertion in a release config test
findings.verification_method: Install a build and read the launcher label, or assert it in app/test/release_config_test.dart. NOT RUN in A1.

findings.title: CI cannot detect platform, formatting, or generated-code regressions
findings.root_cause: The workflow gates analyze, Flutter tests, a web compile, and the SQL/Edge harness. It has no formatting gate, no coverage measurement, no generated-file drift check, no Android or iOS build, no lock-file assertion, no action SHA pinning, and no concurrency or timeout bounds. on.push has no branch filter.
findings.evidence: verify.yml read end to end (52 lines, 48 non-blank, unchanged since 56c1122). Jobs are database-and-edge (npm ci, npm test, npm run check:edge, npm run test:edge on Node 22) and flutter (flutter pub get, flutter analyze, flutter test --reporter expanded, flutter build web --release with placeholder dart-defines, artifact upload). permissions: contents: read is present and correct. Measured consequence: FND-BUG-001 and FND-BUG-002 are both invisible to this pipeline.
findings.expected_behavior: A gate set that fails when a shippable artifact is broken.
findings.actual_behavior: The gate set passes an app that cannot reach the network in a release build.
findings.impact: Release-blocking defects reach main undetected. docs/planning/ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 records 'No Android APK build in CI today' as fact, but no document records it as a decision, so it reads as an unexamined default.
findings.proposed_remediation: In one reviewed CI change: add dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test; add a build_runner drift check followed by git diff --exit-code; add flutter build apk --debug (release needs signing); pin actions by SHA; add concurrency keyed on the ref and timeout-minutes; restrict push to main. TASK_BOARD.md section M1-05 already plans the Android static build and config regression test.
findings.regression_risk: A drift check will fail the first time if generated files are currently stale. That was NOT MEASURED in A1 because running build_runner writes files; measure it before enabling the gate.
missing_tests: a deliberately broken manifest must fail CI
generated-file drift assertion
format gate
depends_on: Land after FND-BUG-001 and FND-BUG-002 so the new gate starts green
findings.verification_method: Introduce a deliberate platform regression and confirm CI fails. NOT RUN in A1.

findings.title: The documented local auth redirect is not in the Auth allowlist
findings.root_cause: supabase/config.toml sets site_url = http://127.0.0.1:3000 and additional_redirect_urls = [https://127.0.0.1:3000], while the app passes AUTH_REDIRECT_URL (http://localhost:8080/ from config.example.json, documented as --web-port 8080 in main.dart:64) as redirectTo in resetPasswordForEmail. Neither allowlisted URL matches the app's redirect target or the port the dev server serves.
findings.evidence: Direct read of all four files. supabase_auth_repository.dart:30-34: const redirect = String.fromEnvironment('AUTH_REDIRECT_URL'); resetPasswordForEmail(..., redirectTo: redirect.isEmpty ? null : redirect).
findings.expected_behavior: The password-reset email is sent and its link returns to the running app.
findings.actual_behavior: Inferred from GoTrue's documented allowlist check: the recovery request is rejected because the redirect target is not allowlisted.
findings.impact: Password recovery is broken out of the box for local development and for any environment that copies config.example.json unchanged. No production impact is claimed; a production deployment would supply its own values, which this audit cannot see.
findings.proposed_remediation: Align the three values. Either set site_url = http://localhost:8080 and additional_redirect_urls = [http://localhost:8080, http://127.0.0.1:8080], or change config.example.json to the allowlisted origin. Changing supabase/config.toml is a configuration change and needs approval.
findings.regression_risk: A wrong site_url affects every emailed link, including confirmation; verify reset and confirmation flows together.
missing_tests: a test asserting the configured redirect target is allowlisted
findings.verification_method: supabase start, then POST /auth/v1/recover with redirect_to=http://localhost:8080/ and observe the rejection. NOT RUN in A1: would start a local stack and mutate local state.

findings.title: Two parallel localization mechanisms, and the standard one carries no product text
findings.root_cause: The Flutter gen-l10n pipeline is fully wired (generate: true, a three-line l10n.yaml, two ARB files, generated output, delegate installed) but carries one key (appTitle). All product text lives in a hand-rolled const Map<String, Map<String,String>> with 104 keys read through translateText/.tr at 209 call sites. Nothing reads AppLocalizations.of.
findings.evidence: Census: app_en.arb is 7 lines with 1 key; app_localizations.dart is 4,839 bytes, _en 351, _vi 354, all tracked and not gitignored; node census of the dictionary reports 'outer keys: 104', "'vi' entries: 104", "'en' entries: 104"; 209 translateText(/.tr(ref) matches across 18 files; AppLocalizations.of appears only in the generated file's own doc comments (lines 14, 24). MaterialApp title is the literal 'GymLevel' at app.dart:21.
findings.expected_behavior: One localization mechanism, so translators, tooling and the runtime share a single source of truth.
findings.actual_behavior: Two mechanisms coexist; the standard one is maintained but unused.
findings.impact: No user-visible defect today, because parity is exact (104/104). The cost is structural: translators and flutter gen-l10n see 1 string of 104; no ARB placeholders, plurals or ICU number/date formatting are available; adding a locale requires editing Dart source and shipping code; generated-file churn is unrelated to product text; a future contributor will add strings to the ARB and see no effect.
findings.proposed_remediation: Choose one mechanism as a decision entry and do not do both. Option 1: migrate the 104 keys to ARB and delete the map, with a plural/placeholder review and a VI diacritic rendering check. Option 2: remove the ARB wiring (generate: true, l10n.yaml, app/lib/l10n/, the app-level delegate) and keep the dictionary, documenting it as the chosen mechanism. The global Material/Cupertino delegates must stay in either case.
findings.regression_risk: Option 1 touches 209 call sites and both locales; a missed key becomes a runtime fallback. Option 2 removes a working delegate that currently localizes Material/Cupertino system strings, which must be preserved.
missing_tests: key parity test over the chosen localization source
depends_on: A2 (C-05) verifies VI/EN rendering and parity; sequence the decision after it
findings.verification_method: Static census of dictionary keys, ARB keys, generated output and every AppLocalizations reference. Measured, not executed; there is no runtime behaviour to promote.

findings.title: The stated timezone invariant is narrower than the per-user implementation
findings.root_cause: The invariant states streaks and quests are computed explicitly in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, but the implementation adds profiles.timezone (default Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh) and computes day boundaries from coalesce(tz,'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'). The zone is per-user, not fixed.
findings.evidence: docs/planning/ARCHITECTURE.md:88 invariant 7 read against every AT TIME ZONE expression in the migrations: progression:3 (column), :198 (quest day), :241 (completion day), :310-312 (stats).
findings.expected_behavior: An invariant sentence that is true of the code.
findings.actual_behavior: The code is more general than the sentence, so the sentence is false for any user whose profile timezone differs.
findings.impact: No runtime defect. A reviewer applying the invariant literally would hardcode Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh and silently shift quest and streak day boundaries for every user outside Vietnam. Same class as FND-ARCH-001, smaller blast radius because no award path is involved.
findings.proposed_remediation: Restate as: store UTC; compute streaks, quests and daily aggregates in the user's profiles.timezone, which defaults to Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Apply together with FND-ARCH-001 so the invariants section is edited once.
missing_tests: day-boundary assertion for a non-default profile timezone
depends_on: A4 owns quest and streak correctness; sequence the wording after it
findings.verification_method: Read the invariant against every AT TIME ZONE expression. Static; nothing to execute.

findings.title: Git approval gates do not match the operations AGENTS.md section 8 forbids
findings.root_cause: The global rule set is allow-all for shell (opencode.jsonc:17) followed by a denylist of prefix-anchored command strings. A positional argument before the flag defeats a prefix pattern; git -c <option> defeats every Git rule; git switch, bare git stash, git checkout <ref>, git checkout <ref> -- <path> and git tag -d have no rule at all.
findings.evidence: 18 probes added to the repository's own evaluator: RESULT: FAIL (12 probe failures, 0 schema problems). Ungated with match [shell:* -> allow]: git push origin --force main, git push origin --delete feature-x, git push origin :feature-x, git push origin --mirror, git switch main, git checkout main, git checkout HEAD -- app/lib/main.dart, git stash, git tag -d v1, git -c core.pager=cat push --force origin main. Gated correctly: git push --force-with-lease, git push origin +main:main, git branch -d, git clean -fdx, rm -rf, psql.
findings.expected_behavior: Every operation AGENTS.md section 8 forbids resolves to ask.
findings.actual_behavior: Six of eighteen probed forms do; the rest resolve to allow. The residual control is model compliance, which is the posture D-019 rejected.
findings.impact: Remote branch deletion, history rewrite via flag reordering or git -c, working-tree discard via git checkout <ref> -- <path>, and tag deletion are permitted without a prompt. The orchestrator's 'Hard refusals' section states a guarantee that does not hold, and docs/planning/SESSION_HANDOFF.md:26 asserts 'force-push stays gated', which the probes contradict.
findings.proposed_remediation: Replace position-anchored patterns with segment-scanning ones: git push *--force*, git push *--delete*, git push *--mirror*, git push *:*, git * push *--force*, git -c *, plus explicit git switch *, git checkout *, git stash, git tag -d*. Then add the A1 probe set to the validator so a missing gate fails a test.
findings.regression_risk: Broader ask patterns interrupt legitimate commands such as git checkout -b and git stash list. Each pattern must be probe-tested before it lands; the validator already supports that.
missing_tests: live per-spelling probe with user approval
depends_on: FND-GOV-003 (matcher semantics) established per-segment resources, which is why the fix must work per segment
findings.verification_method: node a1-git-gate-probe.mjs -> RESULT: FAIL (12 probe failures, 0 schema problems). A live probe per spelling is NOT RUN and must stay NOT RUN: it requires issuing a destructive command.

findings.title: Shell secret gates cover a short list of command spellings
findings.root_cause: File reads are gated for *.env and *.env.*, but shell reads are gated only for four reader spellings: Get-Content, type, cat, more. Any other command that can read a file falls through to shell:* -> allow.
findings.evidence: Probes against the repository's own evaluator: Select-String -Path .env -Pattern . -> got=allow [shell:* -> allow]; Copy-Item .env C:/Temp/x.txt -> got=allow [shell:* -> allow]. The remaining spellings (Get-ChildItem -Recurse, Format-Hex, Out-File, Set-Content, [IO.File]::ReadAllText, node -e fs.readFileSync, git show HEAD:.env) are identified by inspection of the rule list and were not individually probed.
findings.expected_behavior: Reading a secret file resolves to ask, as gymlvl-orchestrator.md:57-58 states.
findings.actual_behavior: It resolves to ask only for four command spellings.
findings.impact: An agent can read and exfiltrate .env, or copy it outside the repository, without a prompt, using an equivalent command. The control is the only thing standing between an autonomous agent and the project's credentials.
findings.proposed_remediation: A denylist over an allow-all shell cannot be made complete. Option 1: enumerate the readers actually used in this environment (PowerShell built-ins, .NET static methods, node/deno file APIs, git show), add a gate per spelling, and add a validator probe per spelling so the list cannot silently shrink. Option 2: reintroduce a per-agent shell allowlist for the read-only and coordination agents so an unlisted command is denied by default. The choice belongs to the user because D-024 deliberately traded the allowlist away.
findings.regression_risk: Option 1 stays fragile by construction. Option 2 reintroduces the override hazard D-024 removed and must not be paired with a broad per-agent allow.
related_tests: the two secret probes in a1-git-gate-probe.mjs
missing_tests: a probe per reader spelling
depends_on: Shares a root cause with FND-GOV-004; fix in one reviewed change
findings.verification_method: node a1-git-gate-probe.mjs, asserting that every secret-reading spelling resolves to ask. A live probe is NOT RUN: it would mean actually reading a secret file.

findings.title: A stale analyzer transcript is tracked as app/analysis.txt
findings.root_cause: A redirected flutter analyze run was committed and never removed. It records 221 issues from a toolchain state that no longer exists and is referenced by nothing.
findings.evidence: git ls-files app/analysis.txt -> tracked; git log --oneline -- app/analysis.txt -> 29f2029; tail -> '221 issues found. (ran in 12.1s)'; current flutter analyze -> 'No issues found! (ran in 2.5s)'; grep for analysis.txt across *.md, *.yml and *.json returns no hits.
findings.expected_behavior: Analyzer output is either not committed, or is regenerated and referenced.
findings.actual_behavior: A stale 85 KB snapshot is committed, referenced by nothing, and contradicts the current gate.
findings.impact: A reader who finds it concludes the app has 221 analyzer findings, including unused_import warnings that no longer exist. It also embeds absolute local paths from the machine that produced it. No runtime effect.
findings.proposed_remediation: git rm app/analysis.txt. If a redirect target is still wanted locally, add analysis.txt to app/.gitignore. Deleting a tracked file needs approval.
findings.verification_method: git ls-files app/analysis.txt is empty after the fix, and flutter analyze still exits 0.
